correctness.rationale: Constant width gives opposite support contacts at distance one, with the segment directed along their normal; modulo π the smooth arc-to-centre pairs partition directions. On the full normal circle the antipodal map exchanges the alternating arc intervals and corner cones. It shifts their 2m boundaries by m, making m odd. Barbier gives total arc length π, and the endpoint-to-endpoint distance 2sin(ℓ/2)≤1 gives ℓ≤π/3. Width one also gives line measure π for normalization. For the load-bearing branch estimate take C=0, A=u_a and B=u_b at the sector endpoints, and positive transverse offset z. Among generating disks only A and B are active at C: any vertex at distance one from C is an opposite contact, on the closed arc centred at C, hence is A or B. Other constraints have uniform slack near C. At z=0 both near roots are zero; their slope difference uniformly is tan(θ−a)+tan(b−θ)≥b−a>0, so the A-root is active there for sufficiently small z. At the far endpoint the C-root is feasible whenever its polar angle θ+arcsin z has not passed b, because the corresponding point is on the arc. The two disks always bound the true chord from above, giving z=O(√ε); the exceptional strip can only be near b, where the A-root slope is bounded below, forcing z=O(ε) for model or true long chords. Its measure is O(ε²). Negative offsets are the reflected argument. This gives the asserted two-sign width integral for every fixed nondegenerate K. The model deficit is z tan x + (1+sec³x)z²/2+O(z³). Outside r=ε^(1/4) the integrated root error is O(ε²/r²); inside, the relative error in xz+z² is O(r²+√ε) and contributes o(ε) despite a logarithm. The scaled root has integral log R+1/2+o(1), yielding each half-sector's ε[log(1/ε)/2+log sinℓ+1/2]. Jensen and the Taylor expansion of log sin give the stated gap. Equal arc angles give equal corner-cone angles by antipodality; the normal-angle pattern then repeats under rotation by 2π/m, so the body is regular up to congruence. The positive chord length is strictly concave in the offset on its support (it is a sum of lower envelopes of strictly concave circular-root branches), so nontrivial levels have zero line measure.
residual_risks: The branch slack and strip constants depend on the fixed polygon. No assertion applies uniformly to flattening corners, disappearing arcs, or increasing m.
